To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamics of sensory complexes are regulated by receptor modification state and temperature.
the stability of the sensory complexes in Es. coli is regulated by receptor modification state and by CheB activity, whereas the cluster core stability is maintained at high temperature.

(a) the exchange kinetics of the CheR, CheB, and CheA/CheW complexes are regulated by the level of receptor methylation and/or by the regulatory phosphorylation state of CheB, respectively; (b) the exchange of CheW and CheA is only slightly dependent on the receptor modification; (c) the core of the sensory complexes is stable at temperatures up to 42 °C, whereas the exchange of CheR and especially CheB becomes faster at high temperature;
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the effects of receptor modification and environmental temperature on the stability of sensory complexes and their dynamics.
the regulation of the sensory complex assembly and its dynamics by receptor methylation, CheB phosphorylation, and temperature.
the regulation of the sensory complex dynamics in vivo and its role in the chemotactic response of Escherichiacoli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of the core of the sensory complexes in E. coli chemosensory clusters depends on receptor activity and on the level of adaptation enzymes CheR or CheB.
the stability of the sensory complex is modulated by receptor modification, but not by temperature.
the stability of the core sensory complex in E. coli is not regulated by temperature, but is regulated by the modification level of the receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sensory complex is a robust structure, and its stability is only slightly affected by the level of receptor activity or by temperature, whereas the exchange of CheR and/or CheB is more sensitive to these parameters.
the sensory complexes are highly stable at the cluster core, and the dynamics is mainly controlled by CheR and CheW, which are dynamically associated with the core.
the dynamics of sensory complexes are regulated in vivo by receptor modification, but not by temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the large cluster size, the dynamics of the chemotactic machinery can be tuned by environmental factors, which can have significant implications for the overall efficiency of the chemosensory system.
, despite a high level of complexity, the E. coli chemosensory pathway is robust enough to maintain its chemotactic response in a broad range of conditions.
, despite the large number of proteins involved in chemotaxis, the system can be surprisingly robust and resilient to temperature changes.
